title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure at the point where a victim decides whom to trust. An AI generated video presented a well known figure from the financial sector as the face of an investment opportunity, and the endorsement did the work of making the offer credible. Nothing in the reporting shows the named person had any connection to the scheme, and the police position is that a celebrity endorsement is not proof of anything.

The fraud did not end with the video. Contact moved to WhatsApp, where the victim was pressed for further payments, was encouraged to borrow money, and was persuaded to open multiple online accounts and hand over remote access to their own computer on the claim that it would help with the investment. That remote access is the part that turns a false advertisement into a channel for taking money directly. Catching it would have required checking who was actually on the other side and whether the firm held Financial Conduct Authority authorisation, which is the check the police advised.

What is not established is who was depicted. The police did not name the celebrity, and the BBC's observation that it has seen scams using other financial figures is not evidence about this one. No finding has been reported against any named person, and the identity and origin of the video's creators are not established.

reports.title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

summary:
A person in the Ards and north Down area of Northern Ireland lost £250,000 after falling for an AI generated scam. The victim saw a video that appeared to feature a well known personality from the financial sector. It promoted an investment opportunity and promised significant returns. After a small initial investment, the fraudsters contacted the victim on WhatsApp and pushed for more payments. They persuaded the victim to open multiple online accounts and gave them remote access to the victim's computer, claiming to help with the investment.

The Police Service of Northern Ireland called this a sophisticated and substantial fraud. The victim was encouraged to borrow money and send funds to accounts controlled by criminals. Police did not name the celebrity, but BBC News NI has seen scams using financial experts Martin Lewis, Peter Jones and Steven Bartlett. Police said celebrity endorsements are not proof. Superintendent Joanne Gibson urged people to stop and check financial activity and families to talk about fraud. Police advised independently verifying who you deal with and checking Financial Conduct Authority authorization.
title_en: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity
